summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship GSD phase 64 ('Rotation Soundness — Revocation Guarantees') for CipherBox, filling four seam stubs in the rotation engine plus hardening the BFS walk against crash-resume and CAS-409 concurrent-add scenarios.
summary.outcome: All 8 plans across 6 waves were executed with TDD (297 unit tests + 3 live sdk-e2e tests passing), the ship-phase pipeline reached verify+secure (both passed), and two soundness deferrals were captured as todos. The session ends before validate/simplify/E2E-gate/CodeRabbit/PR steps.

repo: D-02 re-seal bug lives in the BFS caller (rotateReadFromNode), not inside rotateOne — sealChildReadKey was using the child's own pre-rotation key (misnomered 'parentReadKey') and never writing the result back to any parent's SealedChildRef

D-06: updateFolderMetadataAndPublish used `id: params.nodeId ?? crypto.randomUUID()` and `generation: params.nodeGeneration ?? 0` — silent fallbacks broke AAD stability across all 6 client.ts CRUD call sites
PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY in engine.ts is for the write-body seal role (0x04), not the IPNS publish key — its presence is legitimate until Phase 65, not a D-01 violation

Design §4.5 says double-rotation IS the safe crash-recovery path ('an extra rotation only strengthens revocation'), directly contradicting SC#4's 'without double-bumping' wording; the 64-07 no-double-bump convergence guard over-constrains the design's own model

True mid-walk crash resume with empty completedNodeIds is not viable in Phase 64 because the root is already sealed under readKeyPrime and the resuming host lacks the new key; full recovery requires the Phase-68 IndexedDB durable floor

mergeConcurrentChildren remote-wins policy on CAS-409 re-merge can downgrade an already-rotated child's readKeySealed to the pre-rotation version, breaking subsequent navigation (liveness only — revoked reader already cut at root)
mergeChildren in folder/merge.ts was a Phase-64 stub (not just engine.ts), discovered during research
tsconfig.build.json excludes src/**/*.test.ts — test file type errors are invisible to CI and only surface with tsc --noEmit targeting the full tsconfig
tsup (esbuild) bundles without typechecking — always need a separate tsc --noEmit pass after tsup build to catch real type errors
gsd-tools commit helper reliably reports commit_failed even when the commit lands — always verify with git log --oneline -1, never blindly retry

code.finding: mintFileKeyOnRotate seam filled: generateRandomBytes(32) assigned to node.content.fileKey; contentRekeyPending NOT set (NodeContent schema frozen, Phase 65 scope)
D-02 bug site: sealChildReadKey used parentReadKey (child's own pre-rotation key, misnomer); the fix belongs out-of-band in the BFS caller, not here
D-01 fail-closed guard: throws if !nodeIpnsPrivateKey before publish; the remaining PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY at L394 is write-body only (Phase 65)
verifySubtreeClean implemented: returns {isDirty, frontier} derived from published IPNS truth; stale JSDoc still reads '@throws Always in Phase 63'
verifySubtreeClean only called when completedNodeIds is non-empty — a true fresh-record resume (empty set) skips it and re-enters rotateOne(root), causing AEAD failure
D-02 fix: out-of-band sealChildReadKey in BFS caller writes updatedChildReadKeySealed back to parent's SealedChildRef[N].readKeySealed under parent's NEW readKeyPrime
Convergence guard: currentPub.generation > item.enqueuedGeneration skips rotateOne for frontier children — but root has no parent mirror so root is never skippable this way
D-02 correct re-seal: sealChildReadKey(result.childReadKey, parentState.parentNewReadKey, ...) — confirmed parentState.parentNewReadKey is set from the parent's own rotateOne childReadKey result
item.nodeReadKey.fill(0) zeroed after grandchild enqueue; rootReadKey is never zeroed (flagged by security audit T-64-06f, accepted residual)
merge callback type widened to sync | Promise union for mergeConcurrentChildren async support; backward-compat via await Promise.resolve(...)

@ts-expect-error placed above await expect() instead of directly above the updateFolderMetadataAndPublish call — directive was unused while TS2345 fired below; must sit on the line immediately preceding the erroring expression
CryptoError imported from @cipherbox/core (wrong); correct source is @cipherbox/crypto — runtime passed only because toThrow(undefined) matches any throw, masking the import error

workflow: Concurrent background git commits (e.g., commit helper + subagent) cause index.lock races; always wait for one to fully finish before running another git write operation

lint-staged stash pop can conflict when old stashes exist, dumping untracked directories from unrelated prior sessions into the working tree; recover by restoring the conflicted file from HEAD and moving stash garbage aside before retrying
Running tsc --noEmit as an explicit post-execution step (not relying on tsup) should be standard after every executor finishes — wave-1 caught two type bugs only via the orchestrator's manual tsc run

The plan-checker's research_resolution blocker (RESEARCH.md Open Questions not marked RESOLVED) is a one-line doc fix; both questions being answered in the plans is sufficient to resolve them without replanning
When a plan checker warning is substantive plan content (not a doc fix), SendMessage to the existing planner agent preserves its deep context of all 8 plans — cheaper than re-spawning a fresh planner
Sequential execution on the main tree (no worktrees) is the correct mode for this monorepo: fresh worktrees have no node_modules and would require multi-minute pnpm install per agent
E2E test deviations that work around engine gaps rather than proving the spec should be surfaced to the user for a scope decision rather than silently accepting a weakened gate

friction: lint-staged stash pop conflicted with a concurrent background commit, creating a UU merge conflict in STATE.md and dumping untracked directories from an old phase-3 stash into the working tree — required manual STATE.md restore and garbage relocation
gsd-tools commit helper consistently reports commit_failed JSON even on success, requiring an extra git log verification step after every commit attempt
tsup builds hide type errors since esbuild doesn't typecheck — two type bugs (misplaced @ts-expect-error, wrong CryptoError import source) were invisible until an explicit tsc --noEmit pass
vi.clearAllMocks() vs vi.resetAllMocks() caused pre-existing D-02/D-09 tests to bleed mockResolvedValueOnce state across test runs in wave 4 (64-06 had to fix this as a Rule 1 deviation)

SC#4's 'without double-bumping' success criterion directly contradicts design §4.5's stated recovery model (double-rotation as the safe path), creating a genuine scope conflict that required a user decision mid-verification

The sdk-e2e crash-resume test could only simulate a crash at the final persist call (N=4), not a true mid-walk crash — because mid-walk crash points cause dirty-resume key contradictions unsolvable without Phase-68 durability

rootReadKey zeroization gap: security audit T-64-06f accepted as residual — rootReadKey is never zeroed unlike childReadKey/nodeReadKey
